text: Every grain is five thousand people. When more die than normal, grains are lifted away. As you watch these catastrophes, remember: every generation of your direct ancestors survived all of them, at least long enough to have a child.
In 541, bubonic plague reaches Constantinople: the first great plague pandemic.
In 755, the An Lushan rebellion tears Tang China apart.
From 1211, the Mongol conquests sweep from northern China to Persia.
In 1346, the Black Death reaches the Black Sea. In seven years it kills between a third and a half of Europe.
After 1492, smallpox and other new diseases reach the Americas. Within a century, most of their people are gone.
In the sixteen hundreds, the Thirty Years' War in Germany, and the fall of the Ming in China.
For three and a half centuries, the Atlantic slave trade costs millions of lives.
In 1770, a great famine strikes Bengal.
In 1812, Napoleon marches into Russia. Most of his army never comes home.
In 1817, the first of many cholera pandemics begins.
In 1851, the Taiping Rebellion: a civil war in southern China that kills some twenty million people.
In 1876, drought brings famine to India and northern China. Nearly twenty million die.
In the Congo, forced labour and disease take millions of lives.
In 1896, plague reaches Bombay. Over thirty years it kills about ten million in India.
In 1914, the First World War. Soldiers' grains leave their homes for the fronts where they died.
In 1918, influenza: twenty-five million dead in two years, nearly half of them in India.
In Russia, civil war, and then famine on the Volga.
In 1932, famine strikes Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
In 1937, war comes to China.
In 1941, the war spreads east, and the Holocaust begins.
Stalingrad. In seven months, more than a million soldiers and civilians die.
War brings famine to Bengal. By 1945, the war has killed nearly seventy million people.
From 1950, the United Nations counts every country's deaths, every year.
From 1959, three years of famine in China: the deadliest famine in history.
In the 1990s, AIDS takes millions of young lives.
In 2020, COVID-19 reaches every country. Twenty-six million deaths above normal.
More than six hundred and forty million lives, lifted away.

And yet, every one of your direct ancestors made it through. Each of them lived long enough to grow up and have a child, even when famine and plague took the young first. If a single one had not, you would not be here. Your parents, your grandparents, and every generation before them kept the torch lit, and passed it on, to you.
